authorNote: M1 sample drafted by Claude Code, 2026-10-09; format and content reviewed by Steve Grant, 2026-10-10. Unpublished until the habit's full set is written (M2).

cues.label: Slow down at the decision
cues.text: Pause before each choice and say it as a question: “Where should I start?”

cues.label: Say the tempting wrong idea
cues.text: Voice the first thought your students are likely to have, then check it out loud.

cues.label: Mark the stuck point
cues.text: Use a signal word students can borrow: “Hang on…” or “Wait —”.

cues.label: Keep it short
cues.text: Aim for under two minutes. Cut anything that explains content rather than making a decision.

cues.label: End with the handover
cues.text: Finish by giving students the question to use themselves, and what they’ll do next.

protocol.title: Try it on placement: model your thinking
protocol.try: Think aloud through one problem just beyond your class’s reach, with at least one decision point and one stuck point. Then hand a similar problem to pairs to think aloud.
collect: Two or three pairs’ talk during the handover, noted as close to word for word as you can.
Students’ worked solutions for the handover problem, with any margin notes.
afterwards: Which of your phrases did students reuse, word for word?
Place two or three pieces of students’ work on the rubric. Which level is most common, and why?
What will you model differently next time?
